rounds.text: Clear Secured Services Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at a remarkably low P/E of 6.31x and a price-to-book ratio of 0.82x, well below the sector benchmark P/E of 18.85x [E1, E2, E6]. The business demonstrates elite capital efficiency with a ROCE of 20.16% and an ROE of 18.83%, both vastly outperforming their respective sector benchmarks of 6.61% and 5.09% [E9, E10]. Growth metrics are exceptionally robust, underscored by a 36% compounded sales growth over 3 years that accelerated to 63% over the trailing twelve months, alongside a 106% surge in trailing profit growth [E14, E15, E17]. Furthermore, a DCF valuation suggests a staggering margin of safety of 84.9%, while the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price absurdly prices in negative earnings growth [E35, E36, E37]. Operating margins have also expanded by 2 percentage points over three years to reach 7% [E20]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -10 Cr with a poor cash conversion of -0.33x, and institutional money flow registers as negative [E23, E24, E34].

Despite reported profitability, Clear Secured Services Ltd is experiencing a severe cash generation crisis, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -10 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -56 Cr in March 2026 [E24, E25]. This translates to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.33x, with operating cash flow representing only 7% of operating profit [E23, E26]. Furthermore, institutional investors are actively fleeing the stock, evidenced by domestic institutions cutting their stake from 7.33% to 3.91% and overall institutional money flow reading as negative [E33, E34]. This aligns with an inconsistent operating margin trend across recent quarters and a zero dividend yield despite repeated reported profits [E22, E41]. Conceded: the company boasts a strong return on capital employed of 20.16% and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value well above the current market price [E10, E35]. Nevertheless, the massive capital-work-in-progress build-up of Rs 23 Cr, representing a 155.6% increase, threatens to strain liquidity further before any tangible completion [E30].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -10 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -56 Cr in March 2026 [E24, E25]. However, this cash deployment aligns directly with a massive 155.6% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 23 Cr, representing active growth-oriented capital expenditure rather than structural failure [E30]. While domestic institutions trimmed holdings and overall institutional money flow is negative [E33, E34], foreign institutions actually increased their stake from 3.55% to 4.12% [E32]. The reported zero dividend yield [E4] simply reflects management retaining capital to fuel exceptional top-line expansion, evidenced by a 36% three-year sales growth and a 63% trailing twelve-month surge [E14, E15]. Furthermore, despite the quarterly margin inconsistency [E22], operating margins have expanded by two percentage points over three years to 7% [E20], supported by a comfortable current ratio of 2.18x and a modest debt-to-equity ratio of 0.43x [E27, E28].
